create.name: Integral Yoga Institute of New Jersey
create.bio:
The Integral Yoga Institute of New Jersey has taught the Integral Yoga of Swami Satchidananda in the north of the state since 1969, when a Montclair couple asked the New York institute to help them start classes in their home, with John "Margabandhu" Martarano as the first teacher. After spells in a Garfield loft and on Broadway in Elmwood Park, supporters bought the present house on Maple Avenue in Fair Lawn in 1995; Satchidananda himself came to bless it after a year of volunteer renovation.

Today a team of more than a dozen volunteer teachers leads beginner, multilevel and intermediate hatha classes, each a slow-paced blend of postures and breathwork that ends in guided yoga nidra and meditation. Some sessions are also streamed live on Zoom. The institute adds group meditation, meditation courses and private lessons, and over the decades it has run teacher trainings in basic and intermediate hatha, meditation and raja yoga, with a pranayama training now being added. Workshops on yoga, meditation and spiritual living fill out the calendar, and the institute has hosted a long line of senior Integral Yoga teachers as visiting speakers.

courses.title: Class memberships (in person and on Zoom)
courses.description: Monthly options covering the institute's regular hatha classes in Fair Lawn and online: a weekly-practice pass for one class a week, or unlimited classes for 30 days. Neither renews automatically.
courses.price: Weekly Practice $80.00 (30 days); Unlimited Monthly Practice $125.00 (30 days)

courses.title: Introduction to Meditation
courses.description: A 90-minute class at the institute on several ways to meditate and how to work with the usual obstacles, led by Rev. Premajyothi Devi, the institute's teacher-training coordinator.

courses.title: Private Yoga Classes
courses.description: One-to-one sessions arranged with an institute teacher and shaped around the student's own goals and schedule, for those who want individual attention or prefer not to practise in a group.
